ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

schatzker — pattern 3

An older patient with reduced bone density has knee pain after a relatively low-energy fall. CT shows depression of the lateral tibial articular surface, with no cortical split extending to the lateral side. The medial plateau is uninvolved. Which Schatzker type best matches the CT description?

  1. Type I
  2. Type III
  3. Type IV
  4. Type V
  5. Type VI
Answer and explanation

Type III

Type III: A pure depression of the lateral plateau without a lateral cortical split.

Option explanations

Type III: Type III: A pure depression of the lateral plateau without a lateral cortical split.

Type IV: Type IV describes a fracture involving the medial tibial plateau. The case instead matches Type III.

Type V: Type V describes a bicondylar tibial plateau fracture without complete metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. The case instead matches Type III.

Type VI: Type VI describes a plateau fracture with metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. The case instead matches Type III.

Type I: Type I describes a pure split of the lateral tibial plateau without articular depression. The case instead matches Type III.
